items.title: scikit-learn version 1.9 highlights: Metric at thresholds
items.author: Probabl
items.content:
<article>In this installment of our series on version 1.9, scikit-learn contributor Emily Chen walks through a handy new tool: metric_at_thresholds. 

Most classifiers output a probability estimate (e.g. 70% likely), and turning that estimate into a yes/no decision means picking a decision threshold. So, how do you know what is the right threshold for your use case? Thanks to metric_at_thresholds, now it is easier than ever to explore and identify the optimal decision threshold for your specific use case.

Learn more: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.metrics.metric_at_thresholds.html</article>

items.title: scikit-learn version 1.9 highlights: Callbacks
items.author: Probabl
items.content:
<article>In the second of our short series on scikit-learn version 1.9, Emily Chen walks through another exciting new addition to the library: the callback mechanism. 

Callbacks let you hook into estimators while they're fitting, so you can track progress (even across parallel jobs), monitor scores, display progress bars, and set up early stopping, all without waiting for fit() to finish. Callbacks are experimental in 1.9, with support expanding to more estimators in future releases. 

Emily covers what callbacks are, what you can do with them, which estimators support them so far, and how to get started. 

Learn more: https://blog.scikit-learn.org/updates/release-1-9/</article>
